1: Protection provided against shield damage. Increases by the given factor how much shield damage a ship can withstand before it loses as much shields as an unprotected ship.
2: Prevents a ship from making hyperdrive or jump drive sounds when entering or leaving a system.
3: Prevents a ship from emitting scan sounds.
4: Protection provided against slowing damage. Increases by the given factor how much slowing damage a ship can withstand before it as slowed as an unprotected ship.
6: Energy consumed per second when resisting slowing damage.
7: Fuel consumed per second when resisting slowing damage.
8: Heat generated per second when resisting slowing damage.
9: Energy produced depending on how far this ship is from the star at the center of the system.
10: Heat produced depending on how far this ship is from the star at the center of the system.
11: Strategic scanners allow you to view your current target's distance from you, maximum gun range, maximum turret range, current speed, maximum acceleration, and turning speed when it is within range. The range is proportional to the square root of this value.
12: Tactical scanners allow you to view your current target's crew complement, fuel, heat, and energy levels when it is within range. The range is proportional to the square root of this value.
13: Mobility scanners allow you to view your current target's current maximum acceleration when it is within range. The range is proportional to the square root of this value.
14: Crew scanners allow you to view your current target's crew complement when it is within range. The range is proportional to the square root of this value.
15: Energy scanners allow you to view your current target's energy levels when it is within range. The range is proportional to the square root of this value.
16: Fuel scanners allow you to view your current target's fuel levels when it is within range. The range is proportional to the square root of this value.
17: Maneuver scanners allow you to view your current target's current maximum turn speed when it is within range. The range is proportional to the square root of this value.
18: Mobility scanners allow you to view your current target's current speed and maximum acceleration when it is within range. The range is proportional to the square root of this value.
19: Range finders allow you to view the distance from the center of your ship to the center of your current target. There is no range limit.
20: Thermal scanners allow you to view your current target's thermal level when it is within range. The range is proportional to the square root of this value.
21: Mobility scanners allow you to view your current target's current speed when it is within range. The range is proportional to the square root of this value.
22: Weapon scanners allow you to view your current target's weapons' maximum range when it is within scanner range. Specifically, it shows the longest range of all weapons in a gun hardpoint; and the longest range of all weapons in a turret hardpoint. These ranges include the weapon offset and thus show the maximum range from the center of the ship its shots can reach. The scanner range is proportional to the square root of this value.
23: Thrust produced by engines. Higher thrust increases a ship's acceleration and top speed. The more mass a ship has, the more thrust is needed to achieve the same acceleration.
24: Energy consumed per second when firing thrusters.
25: Heat generated per second when firing thrusters.
26: Shield damage dealt to the ship per second when firing thrusters.
27: Hull damage dealt to the ship per second when firing thrusters.
28: Fuel consumed per second when firing thrusters.
29: Accumulated shield discharging per second when firing thrusters.
30: Accumulated hull corrosion per second when firing thrusters.
31: Accumulated ionization per second when firing thrusters.
32: Accumulated scrambling per second when firing thrusters.
